title: How 9-1-1 Finds You in Canada #shorts
summary: Canada's enhanced 9-1-1 sends the caller's number and address automatically; wireless location uses GPS or tower trilateration; the switch to NG9-1-1 is due by 31 March 2027 (CRTC).
sources: 9-1-1 call centres are operated by municipal and provincial/territorial governments; with Enhanced 9-1-1 the caller's phone number and address are automatically provided; enhanced wireless 9-1-1 uses GPS and/or trilateration (the signal's distance from nearby towers), generally within 50 to 300 meters; text with 9-1-1 for hearing or speech impaired Canadians: registered users dial 9-1-1 and the operator gets a notification to communicate by text (CRTC, 9-1-1 services for traditional wireline, VoIP and wireless phone services): https://crtc.gc.ca/eng/phone/911/can.htm

Revised deadline of 31 March 2027 for the transition to NG9-1-1, an improved service with Internet Protocol (IP)-based capabilities, including text messages based on real-time text (Telecom Decision CRTC 2025-67; kept by Telecom Decision CRTC 2025-291): https://crtc.gc.ca/eng/archive/2025/2025-67.htm

scenes.narration: In Canada, {E9-1-1|enhanced nine one one} sends your number and address automatically.
For cell phones, carriers use GPS, or measure the distance to nearby towers: generally within {50|fifty} to {300|three hundred} meters.
And by March {31|thirty-first}, {2027|twenty twenty-seven}, Canada switches to {NG9-1-1|next generation nine one one}.
Number, address, then a dot on a map.
